raw_response:
I will keep this year simple and practical. I am 72, so I will not spread myself across too many crops. In Quzhou, the most familiar and steady way for me to farm is still the wheat and summer maize rotation. I know this land, I know the water situation, and I know how to manage these two crops without taking too much market risk. I will plant winter wheat on all my land, then follow it with summer maize on the same fields after wheat harvest. I will use improved seed instead of chasing expensive specialty crops, because I want stable yield, good resistance, and work I can still handle myself. I will plough before wheat to turn the soil and straw well, then use rotary tillage before maize to save labor and catch the season quickly. Fertilizer will stay moderate, with more nitrogen on maize than wheat, and I will irrigate only at the key stages. I will spray only when needed, but I still expect a few routine applications for weeds, disease, and insects. My goal is not the highest yield possible. My goal is steady grain, manageable labor, and lower risk.
